simple.meaning: צָנַח (tsânach) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to alight ; (transitive) to cause to descend , i.e. drive down.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 3 times across Joshua, Judges, beginning at Joshua 15:18. Its contexts include family, death.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to צָנַח (H6795).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: צָנַח (tsânach) / H6795 is traced through Joshua 15:18, Judges 1:14, Judges 4:21 as a generated source-based concept entry.

structuredEvidence.definition: to alight ; (transitive) to cause to descend , i.e. drive down

firstOccurrence.englishText: When she came, she had him ask her father for a field. She got off her donkey, and Caleb said, “What do you want?”

timeline.evidenceText: When she came, she had him ask her father for a field. She got off her donkey, and Caleb said, “What do you want?”
When she came, she got him to ask her father for a field. She got off her donkey; and Caleb said to her, “What would you like?”

Then Jael Heber’s wife took a tent peg, and took a hammer in her hand, and went softly to him, and struck the pin into his temples, and it pierced through into the ground, for he was in a deep sleep; so he fainted and died.
